newsitem.title: UK: EU's Kinnock sees end of state aid for airlines.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock sees end of state aid for airlines.

text.p: National airlines may soon no longer be able to rely on vast amounts of state aid, European Union Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Monday.

Kinnock told a Parliamentary select committee that since "open skies" was introduced in Europe at the beginning of 1993, a number of state-owned airlines had applied to the EU and been allowed to receive state aid.
But he told the lower House of Commons Transport Committee that this "period of transition" was now drawing to a close.

"I happen to think that that phase is coming to an end because there is a need for independent, commercially-run airlines," he said, adding: "I have never thought there was a good reason for taxpayers to provide substantial financial support for airlines."

Kinnock declined to comment on the EU's views on a proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines which is awaiting clearance of further regulator obstacles now that Britain has conditionally approved the deal.
"I don't think it would be right for me to give any indications or speculate on this," Kinnock said.
Kinnock said the EU hoped to gives its own ruling on the BA-AA alliance by early March, noting that the alliance was one of six big airline link-ups the EU was considering.
British Airways has said it would complain to the European Commission over what it regards as unfair state aid to troubled Italian flag carrier Alitalia.
